issues.description: Race condition on shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered flag
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request mutates lora_config.is_registered = True after loading weights. The TritonLoraConfig instances are shared across concurrent requests (stored in model_metadata). Two concurrent first-time requests for the same LoRA could both see is_registered=False, load weights twice, or worse, one could mark it registered before the other has sent inputs, causing inputs to omit weights before the engine caches them.

issues.description: _get_lora_config returns None but is annotated TritonLoraConfig (non-Optional)
issues.detail: The signature declares return type TritonLoraConfig, but the function returns None when lora_name is None or lora_configs is None. The annotation should be Optional[TritonLoraConfig]. Also, if model_metadata is None (model not found via .get()), the next attribute access raises AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError.

issues.description: lora_task_id resets to 1 per model and may collide across models
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs initializes lora_task_id = 1 and increments per LoRA, but task IDs are scoped per call. If multiple TRT-LLM models each define LoRAs, they all reuse IDs 1, 2, 3... TRT-LLM's LoRA cache may be keyed by task_id, so two different LoRA weights with the same task_id across models could collide or cause cache poisoning.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path reused for two different paths
issues.detail: lora_config_path is first assigned the path to multi_lora.json (line ~658), then later reassigned inside the loop to model.lora_config.npy. This shadowing makes the code error-prone for future edits and reduces readability. Rename one of them (e.g., lora_npy_config_path).

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the parse loop and print(traceback.format_exc()) in the routers and parse function leak noise into stdout on every model load and every server error. Use logging at appropriate levels (debug/error) instead of bare prints, or remove the backend debug print entirely.

issues.description: Return type annotation does not match returned value
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs is annotated `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but actually returns `List[TritonLoraConfig]` or None. The annotation is stale from refactor and misleads callers and type checkers.

review.summary: The PR adds TRT-LLM multi-LoRA support to the OpenAI frontend, but introduces a real concurrency bug: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered is shared mutable state mutated during request construction without synchronization, so concurrent first-time requests can race. Task ID allocation also resets per model and may collide across multiple TRT-LLM models sharing the engine cache. Several smaller issues remain: incorrect/stale type annotations, variable shadowing (lora_config_path reused), and debug print statements left in routers and the parse function. The test changes correctly cover both backends but the runtime gate around is_registered should be revisited before merge.
